projection.growthBasis: Annual figure used as a constant rate; not projected. H2 Gambling Capital estimate of total global gross gaming revenue (player losses, not turnover) for 2024 (~USD 573 billion), applying ~7% growth to the confirmed 2023 actual of US$536 billion.

sources.name: Rodriguez-Monguio et al. — Economic burden of pathological gambling (Massachusetts All-Payer Claims), J Addict Med

categories.methodology: Approximate mean annual healthcare cost (~USD 9,000) for one person with a gambling (pathological gambling) disorder, from US all-payer-claims data (Massachusetts; 4-year mean ~$9,166).

sources.name: Third Door Coalition — Research and Sources (PSH unit-cost compilation: Culhane et al.; CSH)

categories.methodology: Approximate annual cost (~USD 13,000) of permanent supportive housing (rent plus support services) for one chronically homeless person; documented US program operating costs run ~$10,000-$18,000/year (Culhane et al.; CSH), per the Third Door Coalition.

sources.name: United for Global Mental Health — US$200 billion financing gap report

categories.methodology: Estimated annual global mental-health financing gap of at least USD 200 billion — the additional yearly investment needed to meet mental-health needs worldwide — per United for Global Mental Health (2023).

sources.name: HHS — SAMHSA Awards $255 Million to Administer 988 Lifeline

categories.methodology: USD 255 million — the US federal award to operate the national 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline administrator for roughly one year (annual budget ceiling ~$231M), per SAMHSA/HHS (2026).

sources.name: Laborde et al. — Ending hunger: science must stop neglecting smallholder farmers, Nature

categories.methodology: Average additional ~USD 33 billion/year ($14B donors + $19B LMIC governments) through 2030 to end hunger (SDG 2), per Ceres2030 (IFPRI/IISD/Cornell).

sources.name: Our World in Data — Total shortfall from extreme poverty ($3.00/day, 2021 PPP)
World Bank — Poverty, Prosperity, and Planet 2024

categories.methodology: Annual income transfer (poverty gap) to lift everyone above the USD 3.00/day international poverty line (2021 PPP), ~USD 315 billion/year per World Bank PIP / Our World in Data (the Bank retired the $2.15/day line in 2025).

sources.name: World Bank — The Costs of Meeting the 2030 SDG Targets on Drinking Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene

categories.methodology: ~USD 37.6 billion/year capital investment for universal safely-managed drinking water (SDG 6.1 component), per the World Bank's SDG 6 costing study (Hutton & Varughese 2016).
